Q: is there a way to list all environments (environment names) in R A:

In

Hands-On Programming with R § 8.1 Environments

library(pryr)
parenvs(all = TRUE)

Q: Reverse list Scala A: 
def rev[X](xs: Iterable[X]): List[X] = xs.foldLeft(Nil:List[X])((ys,x) => x::ys)

Q: js and css not loading when hosting next application on GitHub pages A:

I have tried many advices, .nojekyll, different github templates, different folders, branches. It never worked, or the steps were so complicated and confusing - especially for repeated deployments, that it wasn't worth it.

This guide, once set, will work automatically with a push.

How to deploy to github pages

Update: I added a new script below that doesn't require the built files, but the source code and it will build automatically in the pipeline.

Old guide: (still relevent for configuration)

  1. Go to Repo Settings and set Pages > Build and deployment to GitHub Actions.
    Nothing else necessary as the script will be made in the repo in next step.

    • note: only public and org repos are eligible for GitHub Pages
    • e.g. https://github.com/<org>/<repo>/settings/pages

  2. Configure the /.github/workflows/deploy.yml GitHub Action in your repo. Find the file attached below.

  3. Configure /next.config.ts - Find the content attached below.

  4. Add new script to your package.json.

    "scripts": {
  "build:gh-pages": "cross-env BASE_PATH=/<eg-your-repo-name> pnpm build",
}
    • <eg-your-repo-name> is the sub-path where your app will be deployed, it can be anything. I chose repo name for consistency.
    • this value is necessary for assets and links to work correctly when not served from root
    • for example, this is my repo name and the resulting deployment url
      • https://github.com/ackvf/ts-mock-generator
      • https://ackvf.github.io/ts-mock-generator

  5. Build the repo locally with

    pnpm run build:gh-pages

  6. Push the /out/ or /dist/ folder to github to main or gh-pages branch.

  7. This will trigger automatic deployment.

/next.config.ts

const nextConfig = {
  /**
   * Static Export
   *
   * Sets the build to static export so that we can
   * host from any static html hosting service.
   *
   * Limitations: https://nextjs.org/docs/pages/guides/static-exports
   */

  output: "export",
  distDir: "out", // this is the default
  basePath: process.env.BASE_PATH,
  images: {
    // Allows next/image to be used without 3rd party optimization service. - necessary for static export
    unoptimized: true,
  },
}

/.github/workflows/deploy.yml

This flow takes about 20s as it doesn't build anything, it only copies and pushes the existing artifacts. You can use it to push and host any html, not just next.js.

name: Deploy Next.js site to Pages

# This flow requires the built output in /out/ folder. (configure below)
# note: Next requires correct `basePath` for GitHub Pages (see `BASE_PATH`)

on:
  # Runs on pushes targeting these branches
  push:
    branches:
      - gh-pages
      - main      # <- remove main for better control of deployments only via specific branch

  # Allows you to run this workflow manually from the Actions tab
  workflow_dispatch:

# Sets permissions of the GITHUB_TOKEN to allow deployment to GitHub Pages
permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

# Allow only one concurrent deployment, skipping runs queued between the run in-progress and latest queued.
# However, do NOT cancel in-progress runs as we want to allow these production deployments to complete.
concurrency:
  group: "pages"
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  upload:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup Pages
        id: setup_pages
        uses: actions/configure-pages@v5

      - name: Upload artifact
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
        with:
          path: ./out

  deploy:
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: upload
    steps:
      - name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4

/.github/workflows/deploy.yml (UPDATED VERSION)

Unlike the previous flow, this takes a bit longer and it may impose higher cost as a result as it builds your application in the pipeline, tailored to next.js.

name: Deploy Next.js site to GitHub Pages

# https://github.com/actions/starter-workflows/blob/main/pages/nextjs.yml

# note: Next requires correct `basePath` for GitHub Pages (see `BASE_PATH`)

on:
  # Runs on pushes targeting these branches
  push:
    branches:
      - gh-pages
      - main

  # Allows you to run this workflow manually from the Actions tab
  workflow_dispatch:

# Sets permissions of the GITHUB_TOKEN to allow deployment to GitHub Pages
permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

# Allow only one concurrent deployment, skipping runs queued between the run in-progress and latest queued.
# However, do NOT cancel in-progress runs as we want to allow these production deployments to complete.
concurrency:
  group: "pages"
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  upload:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # Next.js app

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'

      - name: Setup pnpm
        uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with:
          version: 10

      - name: Enable and prepare pnpm
        run: corepack prepare pnpm@10.25.0 --activate

      - name: Enable corepack (ensure pnpm)
        run: corepack enable

      - name: Install dependencies
        working-directory: fe
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Build Next.js app
        working-directory: fe
        run: pnpm build:gh-pages

      # GitHub Pages steps

      - name: Setup Pages
        id: setup_pages
        uses: actions/configure-pages@v5

      - name: Upload artifact
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
        with:
          path: out

  deploy:
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: upload
    steps:
      - name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4

Q: No longer see trace/span IDs after upgrading to spring boot 4 A:

Change spring-boot-micrometer-tracing to spring-boot-micrometer-tracing-brave.

So to see trace ids you could use following dependencies in Spring Boot 4:

dependencies {
    implementation("org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-webmvc")
    implementation("org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-actuator")
    implementation("org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-micrometer-tracing-brave")
    implementation("io.micrometer:micrometer-tracing-bridge-brave")
}

Also a tracer implementation is configured if you use starters - spring-boot-starter-zipkin for Brave tracer or spring-boot-starter-opentelemetry for Opentelemetry tracer. But the starters pull additional dependencies.

I guess Spring Boot 3 implicitly auto-configured a tracing implementation when a Micrometer tracing bridge was present (e.g. io.micrometer:micrometer-tracing-bridge-brave).
In Spring Boot 4, the modulesspring-boot-micrometer-tracing-opentelemetry and spring-boot-micrometer-tracing-brave were introduced.
And you must explicitly set what tracing implementation you need by choosing one of them.

Look like it's part of transition toward smaller focused modules in Spring Boot 4

Q: django backend is good shoes to learn now? A:

Yes, Django is absolutely a top-tier choice in the 2026 job market. Despite the hype around newer tools, Django dominates the "batteries-included" space, making it the industry standard for complex, data-heavy enterprise applications, a segment that offers high stability and competitive salaries. Its biggest advantage right now is the Python ecosystem; with the surge in AI and Machine Learning, using Django allows for native integration of libraries like PyTorch or TensorFlow without the context switching required by Node.js. While frameworks like FastAPI are excellent for specific high-performance microservices, Django remains superior for shipping full-featured products (handling Auth, ORM, and Admin interfaces) quickly.

Have a look at this:

  • According to the Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2025, Python remains a top language (used by ~50% of devs), and Django holds a steady share of the backend market.

  • The JetBrains State of Django 2025 shows a surge in developers using Django specifically as the backend for AI-driven applications.

Q: Supervisor usage advice A:

There is no recommendation I am aware of to use supervisor to run the task scheduler. The recommendation is to use cron (or equivalent) and the way that is done is by adding one single line in your crontab file (your script seems much more complex than that to be honest).

Supervisor is used for the queue workers and it is recommended to use that because it can handle spawning multiple queue workers and handle the case where they may crash as well as allowing multiple configuration entries for multiple queue drivers or configurations.

Q: Create clock pulse with python A:

Let's say you want to count in increments of 20ms. You need to sleep for the portion of the loop that's not the comparison, increment, and print. Those operations take time, probably about 10ms based on your findings.

If you want to do it in a loop, you can't hard code all the possible end times. You need to do something more general, like taking a remainder.

Start with the time before the loop:

t0 = time.time()
while time.time() < end:
    i += 1

Now you need to figure out how long to sleep so that the time between t0 and the end of the sleep is a multiple of 20ms.

(time.time() - t0) % 0.02 tells you how far past a 20ms increment you are because python conveniently supports floating point modulo. The amount of time to wait is then

    time.sleep(0.02 - (time.time() - t0) % 0.02)
    print(i)

Using sign rules of %, you can reduce the calculation to

    time.sleep(-(time.time() - t0) % 0.02)
